trajectory_summary: The call opens flat, dips into confusion when the rep over-explains the financial mechanism instead of deferring to the specialist, recovers through a mechanically competent (if slow) bill-collection walk-through, and closes with a clean, calmly negotiated phone appointment. The energy is mixed rather than built or leaked — no rapport was actively damaged, but no real curiosity or emotional anchor was created either; the booking succeeded on procedural competence, not on selling the vision.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (12PM) were agreed for a phone appointment. The son identified as co-owner at 00:45 was never mentioned again or invited onto the call, so co_owner_confirmed is false rather than null.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Over-explaining the bill-swap mechanism instead of redirecting to design
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yeah. So the the way the program works, there's no upfront cost, and you don't have to pay for install.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This single choice triggered the call's only real confusion ('No. I'm not following you.' at 03:55) and required a second, longer re-explanation — a direct, avoidable energy leak that the price_estimate_before_design rebuttal is built to prevent.

key_moments.quote: Now the only requirement is that you have a credit score above 670. Is that true for you?
key_moments.stewart_read: When the customer pushes back on why credit matters, the rep admits 'I honestly don't know. I'm kind of on the bottom of the food chain here' rather than giving the escape-hatch redirect to the specialist.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So the the way the program works, there's no upfront cost, and you don't have to pay for install.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer's direct cost question is answered with a full financial-mechanism explanation (bill swap, inflation, install costs) instead of the redirect-to-design canonical response.
The customer explicitly states the mechanism explanation didn't land — direct evidence that over-explaining backfired into confusion rather than curiosity.
